Application Materials.content:
With your online application you will need to provide:
1. A copy of your degree certificate and transcripts which show you have achieved a 2:2 honours degree in a relevant subject area such as computer science, engineering, finance, management or mathematics, or an equivalent international degree. If your degree certificate or result is pending, please upload any interim transcripts or provisional certificates.
2. A copy of your IELTS certificate with an overall score of 6.5 with 5.5 in all subskills, or evidence of an accepted equivalent. Please include the date of your expected test if this qualification is pending. If you have alternative acceptable evidence, such as an undergraduate degree studied in the UK, please supply this in place of an IELTS.

Application Deadlines.content:
- Start date: **28 September 2026**
- **Application Deadline:** We allocate places on a first-come, first-served basis, so we recommend you apply as early as possible. Applications normally close at the end of August but may close sooner if all places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
- A **2:2 honours degree** in a relevant subject area such as **computer science, engineering, finance, management or mathematics**, or an equivalent international degree, is required.
- For applicants from China: a relevant **four-year bachelor's degree from a recognised institution**, with grades of approximately **80% or above**, is required to qualify for postgraduate taught courses.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
With your online application you will need to provide a copy of your IELTS certificate with an **overall score of 6.5 with 5.5 in all subskills**, or evidence of an accepted equivalent. Please include the date of your expected test if this qualification is pending. If you have alternative acceptable evidence, such as an undergraduate degree studied in the UK, please supply this in place of an IELTS.
Find out more about [English language requirements](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-requirements/postgraduate). Applicants who require a Student visa to study in the UK must present an [acceptable English language qualification](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-requirements/postgraduate) in order to meet UKVI (UK Visas and Immigration) requirements.

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics (MSc) is a **1-year full-time** programme starting 28 September 2026. The programme allows you to develop practical in-demand skills for extracting and handling ‘big data’, with a specific focus on applying data analytics for decision-making in real-life business contexts.
You’ll learn from experts in Cardiff Business School and the School of Mathematics who specialise in applications of data science, operational research and analytics across manufacturing and service industries, discovering and communicating meaningful patterns from data and applying analytical tools to help private and public sector businesses make better strategic and operational decisions.
The programme combines advanced software with core business and mathematical theory and practice, preparing students for employment in an interconnected, diverse and rapidly evolving global business arena. It provides grounding for careers in analytics, data management and consultancy roles.
Key areas include operations analytics, time series and forecasting, strategic operations management, enterprise research planning, risk management, research skills, data analysis and machine learning. Students use real-world advanced simulation systems and games to manage a virtual company in a competitive market, supporting learning through a dynamic business environment.
The programme runs from September to September. During the **Taught Stage** (September-June), students study 120 credits of taught modules. During the **Dissertation Stage** (July-September), students undertake a dissertation project. Optional modules allow students to tailor learning to their interests and career aspirations. On successful completion of the taught stage, students undertake an independent research project focused on applications of data analytics in the real business world and may have the opportunity to conduct a live project, subject to academic performance.
The course is based in [Cardiff Business School](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/business-school), an AACSB International and AMBA-accredited Business School located at Colum Road, Cathays, Cardiff, CF10 3EU.
An employability focus is embedded throughout the programme, including case studies and assessments that mirror workplace challenges. Although the programme does not include a formal placement, students benefit from experiential and work-based learning opportunities such as guest lectures and site visits. Strong links with research groups and industrial partners offer networking and exposure to potential employers. Within the dissertation phase, students may be offered the opportunity, subject to academic performance, to undertake a project with an industrial partner through a competitive process.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
A formal offer of study is only valid for the stated programme of study and start date.
- The date of entry to the programme applied for is confirmed in the formal offer.
- Before applying, applicants may apply for any available intake, which may include deferred entry.
- After an application has been submitted, or after an offer of study has been made, applicants may request to defer their application/place for **up to 12 months from the start date of the programme originally applied for**. Approval of the deferral is not guaranteed.
- Applicants wishing to defer entry for more than **12 months from the start date of the programme** are required to reapply.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you have not yet met the entry requirements, you can usually still apply for a postgraduate course. You may receive an offer of a place on the condition that you meet the requirements before you start the course.
A **Conditional offer** means you have been offered a place, but something is missing from your application - most likely one of your supporting documents or you are still to complete one of the qualifications required to gain admission to the university. Your offer letter will clearly state what evidence needs to be supplied. Once Cardiff University has everything, your offer will change to Unconditional.
Your offer is subject to you accepting your place and meeting the exact conditions of your offer a minimum of **14 days before the start date of your programme**, unless otherwise agreed by the university.
